title: The Next Educated Barbarian Cycle
summary: Final Stoicism episode of the Educated Barbarian book series: NH reads Seneca's chapters on choosing company and on friendship, stressing that you become the company you keep and that true friendship is founded on shared virtue, not interest. He announces the next cycle on Nietzsche, Jung and Dostoevsky.
claims: After about a year on Stoic books, the series moves on; he is not a Stoic and warns against limiting yourself to one philosophy since all have truths and errors
The only good philosophy for you is the one that makes you happy, which requires open horizons and constant learning
Next cycle: Nietzsche (starting with On the Genealogy of Morality), Jung and Dostoevsky, ending with Zarathustra and Demons; expected to take at least two years
Stoicism is not lone-wolf misanthropy; the Stoic loves society as long as it is virtuous and aims at building healthy societies
Humans dominated the planet through cooperation; helping others is biologically rooted, not invented by organized religion
Caring for others includes correcting them with the same severity you apply to yourself: both carrot and stick
Society is a deep instinct, not a social construct; being valued by the group signalled survival
You mimic the company you keep; he has seen good people turn bad after hanging out with bad people
Bad influences near you can get inside you; keep non-virtuous people out of your 'house' or 'temple'
Online advice is treacherous because you can't verify the virtue of people you only watch on video
Once a vice ('the wolf within') gets inside, it never leaves; you can only starve it for life, and relapsing makes it come back stronger
Vices attract other vices; succumbing to one invites more until your life is in shreds, so reject bad influences before they enter
Philosophy without application is mental masturbation and can become poison by making you feel intelligent
The company you keep matters more than the food you eat; the more acquaintances, the more danger, so vet and limit them
A single bad friend can derail an otherwise good person's life
Don't waste energy arguing virtue with the non-virtuous or conform because they are many; push them away unless trying to save them
A friend must be virtuous and the bond founded on a shared love of goodness, not interest; interest-based friendship ends with the interest
Caring for a loved one is caring for yourself; with his partner, each feels bad when the other does
Knowledge is worthless if hoarded; it exists to be passed on
He is extremely selective with friends, can count them on two hands, but once someone is a friend it is for life
If there are things you wouldn't tell a friend, he isn't really your friend
Being with a true friend feels like being alone because you can be fully yourself
He never borrows from friends and gives rather than lends money to them; if you'd lose money that way, you are giving to people who are not friends
True friends tell you hard truths; people praise truthful figures once dead so they need not face them
